With finality the voice says “Mr Dalton, by the power invested in me as an authorised person, I hereby consider this judgement to have been delivered, driver take him away”

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">Hours had gone by, maybe six or seven. 
He had tried counting the time, in seconds and minutes, but when the van left the road and started on what felt like a goat track, he lost focus. It was hard to keep a regular cadence when every bump felt like a hit to the kidneys as his spine compressed on the steel bench he was restrained to.
Certainly the officers… guards… police… he even wasn’t sure who they were anymore, hadn’t said a word since they grabbed him off the street and bundled him into the van. 
Every time he asked even a simple question like who are they, or where are they taking him, the answer simply had been a sharp poke in the ribs with one of thier batons, or like the last time, a swift crack across the head that left him seeing stars. 
Admittedly asking them if they were ok and did they need to stop for a break might have been provocative.
Eventually they stopped, but he didn’t have more than a few seconds to enjoy the blissful lack of movement. No sooner had they stopped, he was unlocked from the floor and dragged out of the van. 
The shackles came off his ankles and legs, the hood stayed on. 
The two guards had an arm each and he was half lifted, half marched to what felt like the side of a road… then unceremoniously shoved. 
That was when he realised he was not on flat ground and where he expected to hit the ground, there wasn’t any. A fraction of a second later he hit a steep slope and rolled… one, two, three, four rolls, then a crash into some foliage and he stopped. 
He could hear the van driving away, as he scrambled to remove the hood from his head. 
Looking up he could see he’d been shoved off the side of the road down a steep embankment and had ended up at the edge of a forest buried in some bushes. 
He assessed himself, what hurt? 
Did he have any serious injuries?
No, he didn’t think so, apart from the pain of bouncing down the slope and being winded somewhere after the second or third barrel roll, he was relatively unscathed.
However, he had nothing on him, he was dressed in the same stolen work clothes he was wearing when they dragged him off the street, at least it was relatively new gear, stolen form the laundry on a few days ago, and they had taken his boots, but that was about the extent of his inventory. No phone to call family, not that anyone would answer anyway, no wallet, money or ID, no food, water, not even a jacket.
He gingerly stood up, making sure his initial assessment of his lack of injuries was accurate, yes all good so far, pretty sure he’s going to hurt later.
He couldn’t see up onto the road down in the ditch, the forest behind him was dark and forbidding, he could see the snow on the mountain tops surrounding him on both side of the valley he was in, they must have gone north.
The Van was long gone, the dust already settling from it’s speedy exit, the noise of it driving away was being replace by an oppressive silence. Having lived in the city all his life he didn’t like the silence too much.
Looking around it didn’t look like it had snowed down here recently, thankfully he was a few hundred meters below the snow line, but the sun would be going down soon and he was already getting cold.</span></span></span></span>

It was a real meat feast cooked outside on real flames on the main balcony, which is more like a full outdoor patio with potted trees and even a grass area adjacent to the six person outdoor table and chair set that sits over looking the city skyscape.
Shane ask Jim “Did you want that last sausage? I think that one is a real beef one”
Jim pats him stomach “Nah… you go for it, I’m stuffed, I haven’t had that much real meat for ages, I’ll be digesting this for weeks!”
Shane chuckles “Tell me about it, we blew through a couple of months worth of meat points for this” he picks up the lone sausage and bites off a big chunk, with a full mouth “but it was so worth it”
Jim smiles as we watches Shane eat that last sausage, satisfied that even though he gave up some real meat, there was no way he was fitting anything more in. Shane casts his mind back to his childhood and clearly remembers his parents doing the Sunday BBQ with real meat quite regularly when he was a young kid. 
The limits to meat consumption were small at first, just a restriction of how much you could buy at one time to stop shortages and allow everyone the chance to buy meat after rolling global supply shortages took most meats off the shelves one too many times. 
Over decades the system evolved to an all inclusive app that accrues what people now call “meat points” or more accurately called the “Government Animal Based Protein Allowance”. The system is very highly regulated, each citizen has a certain number of points added to thier allowance each month, the amount of points you get is based on your citizenship level. 
Points can be used at any government regulated butcher to purchase real meat. If you run out, you just have to wait for the month to click over to reset your points. For most people it’s not an issue as plant based proteins are essentially limitless and mostly approximate the taste of real animal based meat. In fact more people just eat the plant based without ever dipping into thier meat points.
“You can’t bank meat points anymore, I don’t want to know how you were able to buy so much all at once, my butcher is strictly by the book and and won’t go one gram over the monthly allowance”
Shane is licking his fingers for that last taste “You’ve got to shop around, no point just sticking to the one place, there’s always someone will help you out if you help them out.”
“I don’t know man, what if you get caught?”
“Lets put it this way, we’re not sitting here on the 47th floor overlooking downtown if I didn’t ask some questions and bend a few rules”
“I don’t want to know” Jim unconvincingly says as he looks out the window “but I will tell you it is nice view”</span></span></span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1g7jtus r-1x3r274" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">[Idea to fill out - Calorie Warning on Eating]</span></span></span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">Shane glances over to Helen and Sarah, who not being interested in either the football or eating the last of the meat, are over in the dining room pouring over some travel websites on their tablets planning a trip away to the tropics for both couples for the summer break. 
Shane turns back to Jim and points at the 150inch 16k wall panel they are watching the game on. “I didn’t get this beast by waiting in line Jimmy, life isn’t about waiting in the queue with everyone else”
Jim knew full well what the TV was and what Shane having it meant. 
It was one of the new sixth generation TV’s that will be given free to anyone who has enough citizen status points to qualify for the program. 
Much like the previous five generations of government sponsored free TVs, this sixth generation unit is a partnership with the TV manufacturers to ostensibly get old and energy inefficient TVs out of peoples homes, reducing load on the grid and at the same time ensuring the old units are recycled properly.
No one thought too much about it these days, these tech government trade-in partnerships started decades ago and are now available on almost anything
Most people are walking around with the latest free phones, watching TV on their fourth or fifth free TV, banking on free tablets pre-loaded with unhackable banking apps, cooling their food in free fridges, driving in free cars… the list goes on.
The alliance between tech and government was widely credited with raising the standard of living for the average person who now no longer needs to save up for tech or appliances, just sign up to the government program and you get most of the tech for at no cost.
How early you get them, or how premium the appliances were all depends on what Citizenship Status your Points level gives you.
That Shane has a sixth generation unit months before the program will be officially rolled-out to the general public, and that he can get a 150 inch ultra flat wall unit that literally looks like it’s been painted onto the wall and when it is turned off it simply displays the wall behind it in such a realistic way that it’s basically invisible, says a lot about just how high Shane’s status must be.
Jim knew Shane wasn’t level 7 like himself and Sarah, but he’s always assumed Jim was mid level 8, however he was now questioning that assumption and wondering if Jim has been elevated to being a level 9, not that you could come out and ask, that was considered very poor manners.
The downside to the free items from these government programs, which almost nobody noticed, or cared about, as long as they got thier free stuff, is that all these devices were connected back to the companies who supplied the hardware. 
These devices are built hoover up your activity across all your connected devices to build a scarily accurate digital profile that is sold on to the highest bidders, making so much profit that the cost of the hardware is almost an irrelevance. 
The humble fridge now knows what kind of food you like, knows when you need to buy more, when the food is going off, you don’t even need to go to the supermarket. If, as most people do, you leave auto replenishment function active, the food just turns up at your place and your linked bank account is debited. Local grocery stores and even most supermarkets have pretty much been killed off.
Of course the government, as part of the deals cut with big tech and the appliance manufacturers to get them the lucrative tax breaks was, given full and complete access to all the data collected. 
“Aren’t you worried about losing all of this? “ Jim waves his hand around at the apartment. “I can’t take any risks, Sarah is on a mission to get us up to level 8 and I can’t afford to step out of line anywhere.”
Citizenship status is possibly the most important measure of success in society these days, ever since all the various credit ratings, drivers licence points, health status and a dozen other metrics, including what your phone, TV, fridge and any connected appliance was observing, were merged into the one overarching Citizenship Status.
I didn’t happen all at once, but when opting in to the various digital IDs started given people real tangible benefits, it was a very quick progressed to almost universal acceptance that it was the way forward. From there, over the space of a decade all the various government departments consolidated thier systems into one and the Universal Digital Citizenship Status Act was implemented.
There was quite a lot of resistance at first, but the damn broke when the first of the government-private partnerships launched giving away free phones, not just a free handset, but completely free calls and data with the best phone ever produced at the time. The phone was quickly followed up by free electric cars, and within a few years those subscribed to the system didn’t have to buy anything of real value. 
Once the Act was implement, 100% of all citizens were permanently opted in, it was estimated at the time of the universal opt-in that over 98% of all people were already using it.
Jim was enthusiastic supporter of the system and had made it his mission to climb the ladder as high as he could go, that he was sitting in Jim’s apartment having a real meat BBQ from Jim’s account could only be good for his status. Not that Jim wasn’t genuinely a friend, but it didn’t escape him that hanging out with a level 9 could be benefit his own status. Sarah seemed to think so and was very pleased for Jim to foster this friendship.
The game is winding down, a blow out for the home team, and Shane and Jim start talking about a bunch of random stuff just like guys do after a few beers
Shane looks around at their partners to see if the are looking and says to Jim “Watch this”
He goes to the screen menu on the TV and it shows a bunch of channels that Jim hasn’t seen before, some he knows about, but they are restricted so he’s confused as to why they are now in the menu.
Shane see’s Jims confusion and says quietly, so the thier partners can’t overhear “I found a guy who de-restricted the TV, so now I can see anything on here and the best part is it’s hidden from the network, so they can’t ping me for watching things I’m not supposed to see” Shane give a derisive snort “Assholes”
Jim is shocked and a little bit excited, “For real, like fully restricted… I call BS on that, they hard-wire the restrictions into the new units nowadays.
Shane responds “I know, you can get some software cheat codes, I’ve tried them before, but they don’t do anything and the TV just sends a signal back to the network that the software is broken and the next morning the software is reverted back to normal”
Jim ask “Doesn’t that ping your score?
“No, the code just looks like a loading error or some random memory issue so they can’t actually prove anything, like I said it’s doesn’t do anything anyway”
Looking around again he leans into Jim a bit closer “ This is way better, my guy installed a hardware bypass chip on the the circuit board that tricks the TV into thinking nothing in the software has changed, but allows it to recieve any signal or feed, kind of like and old school VPNs used to do before they shut them down, only way someone would find out is they open the TV up, I’ve just got to remember to take it out if I ever upcycle to a new unit again”
Jim is incredulous “Fuck man that’s dicey as hell, if you get caught they’ll clip you hundreds of points”
“Nah, don’t worry about it, no one will ever know, the chip is cutting edge”
“Does Helen know?
“You kidding me, no fucking way man, she’ll divorce me for sure!” Shane says not entirely joking. “You know how she’s all about that top tier credit”
“Don’t I know it… Sarah is the same” 
He looks over to Sarah and Helen at the dining room table pouring over thier tablets absorbed by thier search for travel destinations. “She wants that first class experience you can only get from being a level 8”
 “Level 8? Really?” Shane seems impressed by Jim’s ambition “That’s a shit load of work to get there, are you close?” he asks
“About 350 points away as it stands today, why do you think I get dragged to all those social courses… bane of my life, I’d rather be anywhere else”
“Nothing could get me to one of those things, not even first class tickets, I guess I’ll just have to bask in your glory instead” Shane says.
Both of them know who’s got more points here and it’s not Jim, by a long way.
“If we get Level 8 for this trip the girls want to do you’ll owe me big time!” laughs Jim.</span></span></span></span>

But the cameras are there, silent, watching every inch.</span></span><br><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">Maybe no guards is a final test. Five years since he’s seen his family—his wife and three kids, left behind when he came in. They’re long gone now. He’d had a career as a commercial builder—owned the damn company—but that’s dust too. Seized and sold off by the government, proceeds swallowed by fines and back taxes, they said. Not a credit hit his hands; conviction stripped him of rights to any. A decade of work, profit, a nest egg—erased.</span></span><br><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">His accountant probably owns it now, or so he’s heard. ### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1g7jtus r-1x3r274" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">The first thing he noticed back on the day changed his life forever just over five years ago was that his bookkeeper hadn’t turned up to work yet, neither had his office manager, which was odd as it was the end of month they had lots on that day, it was even more odd as they normally beat him into the office most days.
Must be bad traffic he had thought at the time and made a note to ask his AI to check the traffic reports when he got to his desk. 
He set about turning the office lights on, his office wasn’t so fancy that the lights were activated when he’d unlocked the front door, he was a builder and didn’t need to waste money on fancy office automations. 
He walked through the small reception area by the empty reception desk, which was more of an office prop than functional, he’d never had receptionist, but he thought the dark wood desk and his company logo in embossed glass on the wall behind it gave just the right impression to visitors. That he made the desk himself gave him a little proud moment each morning, he was always sure to give it a friendly pat when he went past it.
He’d walked past the five small offices, flipping on the lights as he went through to the open area at the back of the office where he could set up the big boardroom desk for important meetings. The small kitchen off to the side was also his handiwork, no point paying someone else when you could do a better job for free, after all what kind of builder would he be if he couldn’t showcase his own work.
He remembers checking that the coffee machine was topped up with water and a fresh roast, and then checking if the fridge had ordered enough milk, bread and snacks for the rest of the of the week. The screen on the fridge was showing the order had been sent and would be delivered in a few hours.
This was such a well trodden path that he’d didn’t even need to think about it, what he actually thinking of was making a mental checklist of all the things he needed to do that day. It was an old fashioned habit the his team ribbed him about all the time calling him the human computer, actually more often an abacus if he wanted to admit it. His team all just relied on thier personal AI’s to set thier days up for them and couldn’t understand why he didn’t follow suit.
The reality was he had never taken to having his personal AI do anything important for him, it just never felt right, sure he used it for menial tasks, but never for anything he could easily do himself, secretly he thought relying on an AI for everything was dumbing everyone down.
With the coffee machine still needing to brew for a few more minutes, he walked the ten or so step to his office, it was the closet office to the kitchen, and did was he always did a the start of every day since he taken the plunge and went out on his own, sat down to check his bank account.
The computer had already turned on and ready for him to start work. His watch had notified the desktop terminal he was at the office as soon as he’d unlocked the door. His desktop terminal knew his routine and had opened up his messages, emails, news and  banking apps before he’d even sat down in his chair.
He reflexively clicked through to the banking app.
[Please Log-in again] was flashing on the screen.
Damn, what’s his password he thought, cursing his decision not to let his AI store it. He thought for a moment and it popped right into his mind.
He entered the details.
[No account know under this name]
Damn, he must have typed it in wrong, it was too early for this crap he thinks. Slowly and deliberately he types it again.
[No account know under this name]
Same message, what the hell?
A new email notification pops up from on the bottom of his screen.
[Message from United Banking Services regarding your account]
Ok good, he thought, they are already sorting the problem.
He opened the email and as he started reading he started to fell a chill descend onto him.
“Dear Customer,
We are writing to inform you that United Banking services is no longer able to provide you with any banking services at this time.
As a result your account has been closed and all funds will be held in trust by the bank until such time as the Court orders appropriate distribution of the funds.
This decision is final and no further correspondence will be entered into.
Regards,
United Banking Fraud Department”
Fraud Department, Funds held in trust, what the fuck is going on here? 
He sat still, not moving, barely breathing and he started to processing it all.
He didn’t get to sit for more than a minute or two,  it felt like mere seconds, before he heard loud banging on the office door as someone was yelling through it. The door wasn’t locked. 
Then all of a sudden, a huge crash as the glass door shattered which snapped him out of the frozen state he hadn’t realised he was in.
He got up to go and see what was going on. He didn’t even get around his desk when black clad heavily armed Police rushed into his office, guns drawn and pointing directly at him
 They were screaming at to get face down on the floor, he hesitated for a split second, this was enough for two of them to crash tackle him to the ground. As soon as he went down his face was showed with prejudice into the carpeted floor and his arms were wrenched behind him and handcuffed.
Despite the handcuffs, the pressure on his face hadn’t let up.
An unknown voice spoke from behind as tactical mask. “Neil Lucas, you are under arrest for bribery, fraud and violations of the citizen code of conduct.”
“Under the revised criminal act of the Bi-Continental Government of the Americas you do not have the right to silence, not cooperating with Police will be held against you in a court of law. You will now be transferred into detention where you will remain until the investigation is concluded and you case is heard before a judge. A lawyer will be appointed to you. Do you understand these rights?”
He could actually respond as the weight from at least three or four Police was pressing him into the floor.
“I’ll take your lack of response as a Yes”
It was only when he was being dragged out of the office that the shock had started wearing off slightly that was able to croak out the words
“You’ve got the wrong person, I haven’t done anything…”
One of the Police who is dragging him to the wagon starts laughing at him.
“We never get the wrong person,</span></span></span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1g7jtus r-1x3r274" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">He was to learn later at his trial that this was not mere coincidence, both of them had been working with the Police Serious Fraud Division for months passing on information about his business in exchange for immunity.</span></span></span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">When they said he was under arrest for multiple bribery and fraud charges, his whole world had turned upside down.
He still wasn’t sure what he had done wrong, he understood what he was eventually convicted of well enough, but that he was at fault and deserved five years in prison is something he had a long tine to think about.
What he actually was guilty of was the well known crime of getting duped by a get rich quick scheme. He reflected long and hard about how he’d been duped into the supposed inside track on a new tendering scheme for government contracts, it had just seemed too real and too easy at the time. 
The scheme had worked really well, he’d won some amazing projects and earned some really good money, the profits in his bank account were definitely not fake. At the time he was surprised to win so many of the projects, it seemed he couldn’t lose. He put in his best offers and he had a good reputation in the industry so he took the wins. What he didn’t know was the whole scheme was fake, they were real contracts all right, but built into the project costings were various bribes to unions, lawyers and crooked businesses. The tenders were deliberately set about ten percent above the actual value, the bribes were already built in and just looked like legitimate payments. 
His company was the lead project manager, so when the money was moved around it was done with his bank and his personal authorisation. Technically that meant he was paying the bribes himself.
Now five years on and the only two things he’d worked out was he was too hungry for success and got blinded by the possibility of his plans coming to pass sooner than he expected, he honestly had pictured himself hiking the world before he was forty , not fifty. The other thing he’d worked out was the people that duped him were much smarter than he was, they’d manipulated him from thier very first meeting and then every step of the way they fleeced the projects until he got arrested.
He’d find them eventually.
Standing in the line to be released from prison he was still white hot angry that being duped and set-up had cost him five years and pretty much everything else in his life. No one else was caught, no one else was even charged, the shell companies just disappeared and the money was moved around so much no one knew where it went, not that they tried too hard. 
The judge didn’t care, it was his name on the payments, he was guilty. The trial took less than a day to play out.
It was his turn to be processed now, how long had he been standing there day dreaming?
He stepped forward to the counter. It was staffed by a women in her mid thirties who was dressed immaculately like one of those high powered lawyers you saw on TV, she smiled a million dollar smile and introduced herself.
“Hello, today’s the big day for you, congratulations! My name is Jocelyn Bates and I’ve been appointed as your case worker for the next twelve months whilst you work through your Probationary status, of course if you don’t earn the required points and your probation is renewed, unfortunately I would not be allowed to continue to work with you, but lets not get too far ahead of ourselves. Can you confirm your name please”
“Neil Lucas”
“Lucas… she looks over her files and picks his out of the pile on the counter in front of her 
“Here we go” She’s reading the summary sheet and her eyebrow raises just a fraction.
“Lucas Construction, 12 counts of bribery, 8 counts of wire fraud and an extra six months added for not not pleading guilty, seems harsh”
“I thought so too” Neil quips.
“Please don’t interrupt Mr Lucas and we’ll get through this quicker”
Neil holds his tongue.
Jocelyn is flipping pages on his files making some quick notes, she doesn’t say a word.
She looks up “Well Mr Lucas, all of this seems in order, you’ve served your full term, there was no early release requested, did you not have a lawyer to do that?”
“No, my court appointed lawyer ignored me after I was convicted and no one would take my calls, I’m surprised I even got a case worker”
“All probationary citizens get a case worker Mr Lucas, who you get is luck of the draw, it just so happens today is my day for social volunteering case work. Don’t worry, we’ll get you sorted”
Neil is getting the impression he’s just a box to tick for his new case worker.
She softens a little “Now, I’m informed that your wife has declined to be the post incarceration contact and you have no other family to stay with, is that correct?”
“Yes”
“Ok we’ll get you set up in some temporary accommodation, you’ll receive your full credit allowance into you account as soon as this day ticks over. Just log-in to your personal portal via this new phone” She picks up a box , one of a dozen or so similar boxes that are on the counter and hands it to him.
“That phone is to be with you at all times, no exceptions. Failure could result in you being arrested again. My number is saved on it and you can contact me anytime if you have any issues, now I might not answer straight away, but make sure you leave details when you leave a message. Other than that we’ll meet up one a month at the nominated offices, the address is on the information sheet” 
Jocelyn hands over a folder, the title on the front reads “Probationary Citizen Information Pack”.
“Good luck Mr Lucas, keep your nose clean and we’ll get you through this so you can start your life again”
She ushers him past the counter to the exit with a small wave.
“Thanks” he say says, but she’s already occupied with a new file as he walks past</span></span></span></span>

Section 4, Subsection 3 – Citizenship Status
8.1 Citizenship Status Level 3 (Probationary Citizen) – A citizen that been released from non-permanent incarceration with we deemed to be a Probationary Citizen.
8.2 Such a Citizen will start the probationary period of no less than 12 months without any points, but may accrue points throughout the probationary period.
8.3 If a level of 250 points is not achieved in 12 months, the probationary period will be extended until such a level is achieved.
8.4 Such status will allow access to all government sponsored work programs and approved private sector work programs.
8.5 Furthermore, citizenship points will accrue at 0.25x the normal rate whilst a citizen holds this status. 
8.6 A level 3 citizen yearly credit allowance will be 25,000 fully restricted credits, to be used only for food and lodging, this amount will be over and above any private income earned. Credits will expire after 12 months if not used.</span></span></span></span>

Section 4, Subsection 3 – Citizenship Status
2.1 Citizenship Status Level 9 (Model Citizen) – A citizen that has accrued more than 2500, but less than 3000, citizenship points will be awarded level 9 citizenship status. 
2.2 Such status will allow full and unrestricted access to all Governmental positions. 
2.3 A level 9 citizen will gain priority queueing for all government programs over all citizens level 8 and below.
2.4 Furthermore, citizenship points will accrue at 1.5x the normal rate whilst a citizen hold this status. 
2.5 A level 9 citizen’s yearly allowance will be 250,000 fully unrestricted credits, this allowance will be paid over and above any private income earned. Credits will expire after 12 months if not used.</span></span></span></span>

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">this was my citizenship tier concept....The only and most important things that defines most peoples daily lives is thier citizenship status.
It’s an accumulation of points form the following social entities;
Driving Record, Health status (vaccinations, boosters, weight and exercise habits, lifestyle factors incl food habits) Work status (type of work, industry, management level, performance reviews) Political status (political views, party affiliations) Social behaviour (relationship status, family status, volunteering) Adherence and uptake of government programs and ongoing education in social issues.
There are 10 citizenship levels you can attain, the top 5 are what is called unrestricted citizenship. that means that no services are restricted from you as a citizen, all jobs in private and government sector are theoretically open to you, theoretically there are no items you can’t buy, no holiday destinations you can’t book and so on..
The higher levels just allow you get better jobs, with higher salaries, buy better versions of products, get more from government programs, much like the old frequent flyer programs were platinum members earned more point then gold or silver members.
Yes this does mean once you’re up in the top level you live a life much better than those below and it’s harder to drop down as you earn enough to keep your status, it was designed that way but most don’t really understand that.
The top 5 levels are;
Level 10 – Elite Citizen – They very top 1%, C level managers, owners of major businesses, national politicians, industry leaders. The billionaire an multimillionaire class.
Level 9 – Model Citizen – getting to the top of the business and political world, the upper manager and successful business owners. You have to contribute quite a lot to society to be sitting at Level 9. For many they run almost two jobs, one thier business or political career the other managing all the areas to make up point across all their citizenship status. At this pont many have what are called CM’s or citizenship managers to keep keep them in this elevate level. At any one time only about 10% of citizen are at level 9, most people feeling the effort to get to this level too much work. Many entertainers sit here due to thier influence.
Level 8 – Full Citizen - This is the ultimate goal for people, to attain full citizenship as at this level you can vote and participate in politics. Generally you live a good upper middle class life with all you could want. Many people are happy to stay at this level as it is very comfortable. Middle and upper managers.
Level 7 – Unrestricted Citizen (Permanent) – This is where a good portion of the people end up, a comfortable life without out out trying too hard to climb the citizenship ladder. You get the next level of government handouts, you can get easy promotions up to lower middle management. You are reasonably well respected and have a buffer of points that is anything goes wrong you’re safe from dropping into the bottom 5 levels.
Level 6 – Unrestricted citizen (Probationary) – This is the level that all teenagers children turning 18 are automatically set at for 12 months until they earn start building up a profile to earn thier own points. It’s also the level that new citizens start at. Theoretically nothing is restricted to Level 6 citizen, however practically they are at the bottom of the list for pretty much everything.
Below the top 5 levels, where you absolutely don’t want to be, are the restricted levels where your rights and ability to work and live become more and more limited.
Level 5 – Restricted citizen (Temporary) Quite often new citizens or young people make mistakes, this level is considered a social “slap on the wrist” to get people onto the program of contributing to society. It’s normally a timed restriction for 3 or 6 months after which you’ve served your penalty and you revert back up to Level 6. Most people can ride it out without too much damage done to their lives.
Level 4 – Restricted Citizen (Permanent) whilst technically not permanent this level is for those who have repeatedly dropped below an acceptable level. Likely they’ve committed petty non-violent crimes that don’t give you jail sentences. These people are consistently going against the system.
Level 3 – Probationary Citizen (Temporary) Essentially reserved for those release from prison. These citizens are on probation for a period of 12 months, if no re-offending occurs then they are upgraded to Level 4 Restricted Citizen.
Level 2 - Incarcerated Citizen (Temporary) Status reserved for citizen who have been convicted of crimes and sent to jail.
Level 1 – Incarcerated Citizen (Permanent) Status reserved for citizens who have committed crimes where there is to be no chance of release from jail.
There is one last level, not often spoken of, or even known about by the average citizen.
Level 0 – non-citizen (Permanent) – at this point a person is basically removed from society, you cannot be employed, cannot have a bank account, you can’t travel or use any kind of transport, you can’t own property. You can’t even be homeless in the city as the Police will kick you out of the city or town limits.
This status is so rarely achieved that no one has heard of it. It’s mostly reserved for political and anti-government citizens who have tried of may try int he future to overthrow the system. 
It’s far worse than being in jail, as for those in jail rehabilitation back to full citizen is technically an option, even if it is rare to get back full citizenship status after jail it can be done. Plus in jail you’re housed and fed.
Level 0 means total cancellation of your existence and an inability to even physically be in or near civilisation. you can buy or rent a house, you can’t get money so you can’t get food… basically is a close to a death sentence as society has. Most people who have thier citizenship cancelled just disappear fairly quickly after demoted.
Can other citizens help them, physically yes, but associating with any one of the restricted levels can have a detrimental effect on you own level, so once someone starts sliding down the ladder friends and family quickly start shunning them.
To be helping or associating with a level 0 citizen can get you thrown in jail.
Level 0 do not get thrown in jail, if they get caught they are literally taken far out to the wilderness and left with nothing to fend for themselves. Many level 0 simply die out there.
At the very very top, those who actually run the system, they have no level. They control the system and have basically stepped out of the system completely they don’t ever worry about point or thier activities.
Essentially these are above any law</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">this is the mechanism of how Jim's going to start his fall - The idea is that everything you say in public can be judged. 
The waitress, the receptionist, the people on the table next to you can all get offended by what you have said, regardless of whether you’re talking to them or not.
They can all make a complaint about offensive speech to the local authorities, everyone has the ability to record anyone else.
The authority is simply the Police, who spend more time policing speech than anything else.
The first few times a compliant is made a citizen will get an automated warning via thier government app that they’ve be reported and being offensive in public.
Normally most people just take the hint and say anything the is controversial out of the public arena.
Sometime people don’t take the hint and they are deducted citizenship points for repeated offensive language.
Political speech is somewhat protected, you can support any of the parties that are unofficially approved, there are about 4 or 5 at any one time. You can have debate about them publically, but can;t get too pushy about it.
To a certain degree you can criticise the government, but it has to be done in a relatively mild way.
If you are consistently talking about hot button subjects of the day, or overly criticising the government, or engaging in so-called conspiracy theories then you can get marked as a disruptive person.
A Disruptive Person then has their speech monitored on a 24/7 basis by having to wear a special watch the is listening to conversations at all times. A bit like an ankle bracelet you can’t take it off or otherwise tamper with it, if you do there are more penalties coming your way.
It lasts a year, and if you get no hits you go back to being able to live normally. 
A Disruptive person also has to attend government classes to work though why the are so offense… a kind of perversion of the AA program.
What happens if a person doesn’t comply?
The keep losing points and keep getting thier status downgraded until they end up in jail.
It can also hit your citizenship point status if you’re interacting with a disruptive person.
The system is quite sophisticated, so just sitting next to one on the subway will not rigger and even normal interactions like buying something from a shop, or asking directions or generally having a normal interaction that is common and necessary in a polite functioning society.</span></span></span></span>

Neil looks out the window of the grimy cab that is taking him to his new home for at least the next twelve months. 
He doesn’t recognise the neighbourhood, but he knows what kind of place it is from seeing neighbourhoods just like it on the news, or so he remembers, not being able to watch the news for the last five years.
Its an area of town you avoided if you wanted to keep your status clean, a place where no one over level five wants to be in by choice, back in the day he would have derisively called it the Outer and refused to take on work out here.
It’s no slum, far from it, the government would never let real dirt and filth stay around long, but it’s not the shiny modern city with lush manicured greenery that you might expect these days. The buildings are much more utilitarian, all raw concrete with the very little to soften the architecture. 
This suburb and many other like it is what society says is the minimum you can live with, enough to keep you safe, sheltered and fed, but with little else. What colour you can see is spontaneous street art, not legal, but it’s not worth it to keep covering it up, so it stays.
Neil is taking it all in, the grey drab scenery affecting his mood. He was already planning how to get out of here, and back to his old world, it would be a grind but he always backed himself.
The Cab stops in front of a small four story apartment building, jolting Neil back into the real world.
The halfway house is a nondescript grey box on a nondescript street, but at least he can see a supermarket and a few shops close by, something to explore once he’s settled in.</span></span></span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">He’s greeted at the door by a messy man, tall and quite round, with five day growth about as long as his buzz cut. He’s cleat not soft as his handshake almost crushes Neil’s hand as he introduces himself.
“Hi, Neil? I’m Grant the House Manager, we’ve been expecting you”
He gesture Neil inside “Welcome to your new home, lets go in”
Once inside Grant ushers Neil past the small foyer and reception area into his office. It’s surprisingly clean and well organised, the terminal is pretty late model and the furnishing is new enough to still give off a faint factory smell.
In fact the whole place smells a bit antiseptic.
“Take a seat Neil, congratulations on your first day of freedom!”
Neil laughs “Thanks, was nice to see the back of the prison”
“I’m sure, I’m Sure.. now lets get you booked in and sorted out, I’m going to run through as few things here for you, standard orientation stuff, but I’m legally obliged to record this and your responses, are you ready?
“Yep, shoot”
Grant takes a beat with Neil’s turn of phrase “For the purposed of the recording Yes is all I need you hear ok?
“Yes”
“Good” Grant presses record on his terminal and start reading off the screen. 
“Neil, based on the severity of your crimes and the length of you incarceration, you have been assigned to this transitional accommodation for a period of no less than twelve months.
“At the end of the twelve month we hope you have done enough work to be able to vacate this facility and reintegrate fully into society as a productive and lawful citizen.”
If you have not fulfilled earned the right to be reintegrated, you will be moved to a more permanent situation supplied by the government. Do you understand?”
“Yes” Neil answers.
“This facility is not free, as part of your path to becoming a productive citizen, it is important that you pay your own way, to that end the costs of living here will accrue for the next twelve months and be converted into a government loan. After twelve months interest, which has been set at the nominal federal rate, will be applied until the loan is paid off. Do you understand?”
Neil was shocked, no one had mentioned this “How much does this place cost?
A raised eyebrow from Grant “Yes only”
“Yes”
Grant continues “You will be assigned employment based on your skill profile, you are expected to remain employed in that role for the full duration of twelve months. do you understand?
“Yes”
Grant clicks a button on the terminal “Ok, that’s done, official part is over… sorry about that it always surprises me how little they tell you about life after prison. If it’s any consolation I didn’t know either”
“You were in jail?”
Grant waves his hand “it was a while ago but nothing changed it seems. Let get you settled in to your room”
“So how much will I owe at the end of my time here? how and I supposed to build back up?” Neil asks as they leave the office and head to the lift.
“I don’t get to see that info, it’s different for everyone, all depends on what you did and who you were before. It’s all on that new phone they gave you, you just have to look it up”
They stop on the third floor, Grant walks Neil to one of the eight apartments on the floor, 307 and opens up the door. “It’s coded to you, and also to me if I need to go in for any reason, although I never do. The bus will be out the front at 7am sharp to take you to work, don’t be late. There’s some food in kitchen, my welcome gift to you, and some work clothes that should fit you, you’ll have your monthly credit in your account now so from now on anything you want is all up to you.
Neil steps in to the apartment and asks “Work, where am I working?”
“ Like I said, I don’t get to know that, just get on the bus tomorrow at 7qm sharp… oh and the curfew here is 8pm, which was about twenty minutes ago, so you’re in for the night now, but the rec room is open all night,it’s just behind the reception downstairs.” 
Damn, Neil was looking forward to taking a walk later, and he had so many more questions for Grant, but he was already back down to corridor getting in the lift.</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">did a rewrite adding some more colour: The sleek dark grey late model EV rolls near silent through the city streets, Jim is sitting relaxed at the wheel, not even looking where the car is taking him. 
The car is seamlessly cutting through the traffic, the streets are buzzing with activity, inside the cocoon of the real leather lined car the noise and activity outside doesn’t penetrate enough to disturb Jim from his thoughts.
The car slides past perfectly clean, sleek marble and glass buildings cut through by immaculately manicured gardens, the dusk sun glinting gold off the mirrored facades of the high rise buildings. None of the Outer’s drab grey utilitarian suburbs here.
The car alerts and takes a quick swerve jolting Jim and his wife out of their collective musing, Jim’s wife sitting next to him squeals as she looses hold of the tablet she’d been using to search for holiday destinations.
Jim, taking hold of the wheel reflexively, not that it helps, the car has better reactions times. He see the problem a work truck pulled off the curb without looking and caused all the around to evade it.
“Damn manual drivers, probability some probationer” Jim mutters using the derogatory term for those who are stuck in menial work.
Helen picks up the tablet checking it’s ok.
“Jim, be careful, language!” she scolds sharply.
She looks up from the tablet taking in the streetscape.
“This really is the big end of town, just look at all the money here” Sarah now getting excited about the evening ahead “I’ve been dying to seeing Shane and Helen’s new place for months, I’m still dissapointed we didn’t get an invite to the house warming”
“Yep, you can smell the status here can’t you, this is where you’d want to be” Jim says just a bit too lightly ignoring the dig that he couldn’t secure the invite.
They both know this is exactly where they want to be, meeting up with Shane at his new place is a big deal for thier plans to climb the ladder, a BBQ with someone like Shane can make things move in the right direction and fast.
“Are you and Helen still talking about the Europe trip?” Jim asks.
“Yes, Helen’s keen on Italy, I’d like France, but it all depends on what kind status we can get with Shane being a Level 9 now… of course Helen didn’t say if he was there or not, she’s keeping that one quiet, but everyone’s got to know right? I mean she was talking about first class ticket for us all, a level 8 can’t afford do that for four people.
“We can barely afford economy right now” Jims says, his mood shifts slightly as his reality as a Level 7 citizen creeps in. 
Shaking the mood off Jim, gets excited again ”a free First class holiday to Europe with a Level 9, guess what, we go wherever Helen wants to go!”
The car softly chimes they have arrived with thier destination, the screen on the console reads: Level 8/9 restricted building, temporary level 7 guest access granted.
Jim raises his eyebrow at Helen as they read the message at the same time “Here we go”
Helen chuckles excitedly, this is going to be an important night for both of them.</span></span></span></span>

No need to re-wtire this just give me notes The sleek dark grey late model EV rolls near silent through the city streets, Jim is sitting relaxed at the wheel, not even looking where the car is taking him. 
The car is seamlessly cutting through the traffic, the streets are buzzing with activity, inside the cocoon of the real leather lined car the noise and activity outside doesn’t penetrate enough to disturb Jim from his thoughts, the street nosies pleasantly muffled by the active noise cancelling system.
The car slides past perfectly clean, sleek marble and glass buildings cut through by immaculately manicured gardens of millimetre perfect hedges and impossibly bright flora displays. the dusk sun glinting bronze gold off the mirrored facades of the high rise buildings lined the billiard smooth street. 
Certainly none of the Outer’s drab grey oppressive utilitarian suburbs here, Jim has worked hard for years to have left that world behind.
The car alerts and takes a fast and violent swerve, jolting Jim and his wife out of their collective musing, Jim’s wife sitting next to him squeals loudly as she looses hold of the tablet she’d been using to search for holiday destinations.
Jim, takes hold of the wheel reflexively, not that it helps, the car has better reactions times then he could ever have. He sees the problem, a work truck pulled off the curb without looking and caused all the around to evade it.
“Damn manual drivers, probability some probationer” Jim mutters using the derogatory term for those who are stuck in menial work. “ Why can’t they just go auto drive like everyone else”
The truck pulls away down a side street, it was a sanitary systems truck.
“At least we can’t smell it” says Jim as he watches is disappear into another building.
Helen picks up the tablet checking it’s ok.
“Jim, be careful, language!” she scolds sharply. “You don’t want anymore speech warnings, not with all the work we’ve done to get to here” Helen gestures around the opulent car interior not looking up from the tablet.
Jim shrugs, this is old territory.
Taking notice of the streetscape Sarah says “This really is the big end of town, just look at all the money here” now getting excited about the evening ahead “I’ve been dying to seeing Shane and Helen’s new place for months, I’m still dissapointed we didn’t get an invite to the house warming”
“Yep, you can smell the status here can’t you, this is where you’d want to be” Jim says just a bit too lightly ignoring the dig that he couldn’t secure the invite.
They both know this is exactly where they want to be, meeting up with Shane at his new place is a big deal for thier plans to climb the ladder, a BBQ with someone like Shane can make things move in the right direction and fast.
“Are you and Helen still talking about the Europe trip?” Jim asks.
“Yes, Helen’s keen on Italy, I’d like France, but it all depends on what kind status we can get with Shane being a Level 9 now… of course Helen didn’t say if he was there or not, she’s keeping that one quiet, but everyone’s got to know right? I mean she was talking about first class ticket for us all, a level 8 can’t afford do that for four people.
“We can barely afford economy right now” Jims says, his mood shifts slightly as his reality as a Level 7 citizen creeps in. 
Shaking the mood off Jim, gets excited again ”a free First class holiday to Europe with a Level 9, guess what, we go wherever Helen wants to go!”
The car softly chimes they have arrived with thier destination, the screen on the console reads: Level 8/9 restricted building, temporary level 7 guest access granted.
Jim raises his eyebrow at Helen as they read the message at the same time “Here we go”
Helen chuckles excitedly, this is going to be an important night for both of them.</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">revised the next section, added more colur, added more snap to Shane's hook and jim taking the bait, and showed shane's mask slipping ever so slightly...  the last third might be a bit wordy ;Jim and Shane are lounging in the living room, basking in the aftermath of the BBQ, watching the football game on Shane’s brand new 16k 200 inch TV.
The view from the lounge is no less impressive as the neon lights of the city below them waxes and wanes with huge full colour screens advertising everything from the next new phone or car, to the healthiest soft drink ever made to the latest new housing development. Building lights twinkles all around them as other people go on about thier lives, but here up in the Shane’s penthouse, it all seems so calm with the rest of the world so far beneath them.
The doors to the garden are open and the soft rumble of city sounds drift in with the cooling breeze, the occasion blaring horn punctuation the relaxing hum.
Shane ask Jim “Did you want that last sausage? I think that one is a real beef one” and points to the plate on the low marble table in front of them.
Jim pats him stomach “Nah… you go for it, I’m stuffed, I haven’t had that much real meat for ages, I’ll be digesting this for weeks!”
Shane chuckles “Tell me about it, I blew through a couple of months worth of meat points for this” he picks up the lone sausage and bites off a big chunk, with a full mouth “but it was so worth it”
Jim smiles as we watches Shane eat that last sausage, satisfied that even though he gave up some real meat, there was no way he was fitting anything more in. 
Shane casts his mind back to his childhood and clearly remembers his parents doing the Sunday BBQ with real meat when he was a young kid, that’s got to be thirty years ago now.
The limits to meat consumption were small at first, just a restriction of how much you could buy at one time to stop so-called shortages and allow everyone the equal chance to buy meat after rolling global supply issues took most meats off the shelves one too many times. 
Over decades the system evolved to an all inclusive app that accrues what people now call “meat points” or more accurately called the “Government Animal Based Protein Allowance”. 
The system is very highly regulated, each citizen has a certain number of points added to thier allowance each month, the amount of points you get is based on your citizenship level. Jim can afford real meat once or twice every month on his Level 7 allowance.
Points can be used at any government regulated butcher to purchase real meat. If you run out, you just have to wait for the month to click over to reset your points. For most people it’s not an issue as plant based proteins are essentially limitless and free from the government and mostly approximate the taste of real animal based meat. 
In fact more people just eat the plant based without ever dipping into thier meat points.
“You can’t bank meat points anymore, I don’t want to know how you were able to buy so much all at once, my butcher is strictly by the book and and won’t go one gram over the monthly allowance”
Shane is licking his fingers for that last taste “You’ve got to shop around, no point just sticking to the one place, there’s always someone will help you out if you help them out.”
“I don’t know man, what if you get caught?”
“Lets put it this way, we’re not sitting here on the 47th floor overlooking downtown if I didn’t ask some questions and bend a few rules”
“I don’t want to know” Jim unconvincingly says as he looks out the window “but I will tell you it is nice view”
Just as Jim is contemplating how you could even bend the rules, his phone gently pings that he has a message from his health app.
[Calorie Alert – you have consumed well above the recommended daily intake of protein and fats. You will need to adjust your diet and exercise regime for the rest of the week. A new menu and work-out program has been uploaded for you. Remember your health is your responsibility]
“Damn it, now I’ll be on oatmeal for the rest of the week” says Jim exasperated.
He notices, Shane’s phone doesn’t ping.
“Hey how did you avoid a calorie alert?
Shane leans in conspiratorially with a wry smile “Can’t exceed your limit if it doesn’t know what you’ve eaten”
Jim is genuinely shocked, over allowance meat purchase and now no calorie alert.
“Shane that’s dangerous territory, even for you”
Shane glances over to Helen and Sarah, who not being interested in either the football or eating the last of the meat, are in the dining room pouring over some travel websites on their tablets planning the trip to Italy.
“Don’t worry Jim, we’re safe in here, like I said, if they don’t know what your doing they can’t ping you.”
Shane turns back to Jim and points at the 200inch 16k wall panel they are watching the game on.
“I didn’t get the meat, this beast, or even the apartment by waiting in line like everyone else Jim, real life isn’t about waiting in the queue”
Jim knew full well what the TV was and what Shane having it meant. 
It was one of the new generation 16k TV’s that will be given free to anyone who has enough citizen status points to qualify for the program. Watching the game you feel like you are quite literally standing on the sidelines yourself.
Much like the previous generations of government sponsored free TVs, this next generation unit was a partnership with the TV manufacturers and the Government to ostensibly get old and energy inefficient TVs out of peoples homes, reducing load on the grid and at the same time ensuring the old units are recycled properly.
No one thought too much about it these days, these tech-government trade-in partnerships started decades ago and are now available on almost anything
Most people were walking around with the latest free phones, watching TV on their fourth or fifth free TV, banking on free tablets pre-loaded with unhackable banking apps, cooling their food in free fridges, driving in free cars… the list goes on.
The alliance between tech and government was widely credited with raising the standard of living for the average person who no longer needs to save up for tech or appliances, just sign up to the government program and you get most of the tech at no cost.
How early you get them, or how premium the appliances were all depends on what Citizenship Status your Points level gives you.
That Shane has a next generation unit months before the program will be officially rolled-out to the general public, and that he can get a 200inch wall unit that is so thin when it is turned off it simply displays the wall behind it in such a realistic way that it’s invisible, says a lot about just how high Shane’s status must be now. 
Not that you could come out and ask, that would be a step too far, most people kept thier point quiet, but you could mostly work out where someone was pretty quickly.
The downside to the free items from these government programs, which almost nobody noticed, or cared about, as long as they got thier free stuff, is that all these devices were connected back to the companies who supplied the hardware. 
The devices are built siphon up your activity across all your connected devices to build a scarily accurate digital profile that is sold on to the highest bidders, making so much profit that the cost of the hardware is almost an irrelevance. 
Even the humble fridge now knows what kind of food you like, knows when you need to buy more, when the food is going off, you don’t even need to go to the supermarket. If, as most people do, you leave auto replenishment function active, the food just turns up at your place and your linked bank account is debited. Local grocery stores and even most supermarkets have pretty much been killed off.
Of course the government, as part of the deals cut with big tech and the appliance manufacturers to get them the lucrative tax breaks was, given full and complete access to all the data collected. 
Shane can see Jim’s mind turning over “I can see those wheels turning Jimmy, go on ask, it’s ok”
“Aren’t you worried about losing all of this? “ Jim waves his hand around at the apartment. “I can’t take any risks, Sarah is on a mission to get us up to level 8 and I can’t afford to step out of line anywhere.”
Citizenship status is possibly the most important measure of success in society these days, ever since all the various credit ratings, drivers licence points, health status and a dozen other metrics, including what your phone, TV, fridge and any connected appliance was observing, were merged into the one overarching Citizenship Status.
I didn’t happen all at once, but when opting in to the various digital IDs started given people real tangible benefits, it was a very quick progressed to almost universal acceptance that it was the way forward. From there, over the space of a decade all the various government departments consolidated thier systems into one and the Universal Digital Citizenship Status Act was implemented.
There was quite a lot of resistance at first, but the damn broke when the first of the government-private partnerships launched giving away free phones, not just a free handset, but completely free calls and data with the best phone ever produced at the time. The phone was quickly followed up by free electric cars, and within a few years those subscribed to the system didn’t have to buy anything of real value. 
Once the Act was implement, 100% of all citizens were permanently opted in, it was estimated at the time of the universal opt-in that over 98% of all people were already using it.
Jim was enthusiastic supporter of the system and had made it his mission to climb the ladder as high as he could go, that he was sitting in Jim’s apartment having a real meat BBQ from Jim’s account could only be good for his status. Not that Jim wasn’t genuinely a friend, but it didn’t escape him that hanging out with someone of his status could be benefit to his own status. Sarah seemed to think so and was very pleased for Jim to foster this friendship.
Shane leans forward a bit more, his smile and relaxed demeanour hardens slightly.
“That wasn’t what you want to ask was it? Go on ask, I dont mind”
Jim feeling the pressure of Shane’s charisma ask “Are you level 9? is this how you get all this stuff, the apartment, the meat, all of it?
Shane looks around again to their wives to see if the are looking and says to Jim “Sure I’m a level 9, I have been for ages, but I didn’t get there and all the extra perks by following the rules, watch this”
He goes to the screen menu on the TV and it shows a bunch of channels that Jim hasn’t seen before, some he knows about, but they are restricted so he’s confused as to why they are now in the menu.
Shane see’s Jims confusion and says quietly, so the thier partners can’t overhear “I know a guy who de-restricted the TV, so now I can see anything on here and the best part is it’s hidden from the network, so they can’t ping me for watching things I’m not supposed to see” Shane give a derisive snort “Assholes”
Jim is shocked and a little bit excited, “For real, like fully restricted… I call BS on that, they hard-wire the restrictions into the new units nowadays.
Shane responds “I know, you can get some software cheat codes, I’ve tried them before, but they don’t do anything and the TV just sends a signal back to the network that the software is broken and the next morning the software is reverted back to normal”
Jim ask “Doesn’t that ping your score?
“No, the code just looks like a loading error or some random memory issue so they can’t actually prove anything, like I said it’s doesn’t do anything anyway”
Looking around again, he continues “This is way better, my guy installed a hardware bypass chip on the the circuit board that tricks the TV into thinking nothing in the software has changed, but allows it to recieve any signal or feed, kind of like the old school VPNs used to do before they shut them down, only way someone would find out is they open the TV up, I’ve just got to remember to take it out if I ever upcycle to a new unit again”
Jim is incredulous “Fuck man that’s dicey as hell, if you get caught they’ll clip you hundreds of points”
“Nah, don’t worry about it, no one will ever know, the chip is cutting edge”
“Does Helen know?
“You kidding me, no fucking way man, she’ll divorce me for sure!” Shane says not entirely joking. “You know how she’s all about that top tier credit”
“Don’t I know it… Sarah is the same” 
He looks over to Sarah and Helen at the dining room table pouring over thier tablets absorbed by thier search for travel destinations. “She wants that first class experience you can only get from being a level 8”
 “Level 8? Really?” Shane seems impressed by Jim’s ambition “That’s a shit load of work to get there, are you close?” he asks
“About 350 points away as it stands today, why do you think I get dragged to all those social courses… bane of my life, I’d rather be anywhere else”
“Nothing could get me to one of those things, not even first class tickets, I guess I’ll just have to bask in your glory instead” Shane says.
Both of them know who’s got more points here and it’s not Jim, by a long way.
“If we get Level 8 for this trip the girls want to do you’ll owe me big time!” laughs Jim.</span></span></span></span>

### User

<span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi" style="direction: ltr;"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">It was one of the new generation 16k TV’s that will be given free to anyone who has enough citizen status points to qualify for the program. Watching the game you feel like you are quite literally standing on the sidelines yourself.
Much like the previous generations of government sponsored free TVs, this next generation unit was a partnership with the TV manufacturers and the Government to ostensibly get old and energy inefficient TVs out of peoples homes, reducing load on the grid and at the same time ensuring the old units are recycled properly.
No one thought too much about it these days, these tech-government trade-in partnerships started decades ago and are now available on almost anything
Most people were walking around with the latest free phones, watching TV on their fourth or fifth free TV, banking on free tablets pre-loaded with unhackable banking apps, cooling their food in free fridges, driving in free cars… the list goes on.
The alliance between tech and government was widely credited with raising the standard of living for the average person who no longer needs to save up for tech or appliances, just sign up to the government program and you get most of the tech at no cost.
How early you get them, or how premium the appliances were all depends on what Citizenship Status your Points level gives you.
That Shane has a next generation unit months before the program will be officially rolled-out to the general public, and that he can get a 200inch wall unit that is so thin when it is turned off it simply displays the wall behind it in such a realistic way that it’s invisible, says a lot about just how high Shane’s status must be now. 
Not that you could come out and ask, that would be a step too far, most people kept thier point quiet, but you could mostly work out where someone was pretty quickly.
The downside to the free items from these government programs, which almost nobody noticed, or cared about, as long as they got thier free stuff, is that all these devices were connected back to the companies who supplied the hardware. 
The devices are built siphon up your activity across all your connected devices to build a scarily accurate digital profile that is sold on to the highest bidders, making so much profit that the cost of the hardware is almost an irrelevance. 
Even the humble fridge now knows what kind of food you like, knows when you need to buy more, when the food is going off, you don’t even need to go to the supermarket. If, as most people do, you leave auto replenishment function active, the food just turns up at your place and your linked bank account is debited. Local grocery stores and even most supermarkets have pretty much been killed off.
Of course the government, as part of the deals cut with big tech and the appliance manufacturers to get them the lucrative tax breaks was, given full and complete access to all the data collected.</span></span></span></span>
